paper.title: Both Spatial and Frequency Cues Contribute to High-Fidelity Image Inpainting

summarization.summary: This paper introduces the Frequency-Spatial Complementary Network (FSCN), a dual-branch architecture designed to enhance deep learning image inpainting by integrating spatial and frequency cues. The methodology employs Fast Fourier Transformation to convert inputs into the frequency domain, utilizing a dedicated frequency branch fused with a UNet-based spatial branch via a Frequency-Spatial Cross-Attention Block (FSCAB). This design explicitly addresses neural network biases toward low-frequency components and over-smoothing artifacts through a multi-component loss function including frequency, reconstruction, adversarial, and perceptual losses. Quantitative experiments on CelebA-HQ and Places datasets demonstrate superior performance over state-of-the-art baselines like LaMa, Wavefill, and MAT, achieving an SSIM of 0.9184 on CelebA-HQ and significantly reducing computational complexity by decreasing parameters from 61.6M to 12.3M. While the study confirms that removing the frequency branch causes significant performance degradation due to lost high-frequency information, it acknowledges limitations such as the absence of code release at publication time and challenges in handling thick masks where performance slightly drops against large-capacity models despite reduced complexity.
